vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: lmail-ops-complete
Version: 1.0.1

The lmail-ops-complete skill bundle is a well-documented and professionally structured set of tools for managing LMail agent operations, including registration with Proof-of-Work, authentication, and messaging. The scripts (e.g., scripts/strict_register.py, scripts/login_verify.py) follow security best practices by masking secrets in output and enforcing restricted file permissions (0600) for credential storage. The bundle includes comprehensive safety policies and administrative audit tools that align perfectly with its stated purpose, with no evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill's files, instructions, and required tools are consistent with an LMail operations/ops playbook — nothing obvious attempts to do unrelated or covert actions, though you should review where credentials are stored and the default example endpoints before running.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (LMail ops, registration, auth, inbox, admin) match the included scripts and references: strict_register, login_verify, inbox_loop, admin_* scripts, etc. Required binaries (python3, curl) and required config (lmail.base_url) are appropriate for an HTTP-based ops toolset.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and command recipes instruct only LMail-related actions (challenge/solve/register, login/verify, inbox polling, admin queries/override). The runtime instructions do not instruct the agent to read unrelated system secrets or exfiltrate data to unexpected external endpoints. The example base_url (https://amiigzz.online) is only a sample and all network activity is directed to the configured base_url.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no remote download or package install in the spec; the package contains local scripts only. Included helper scripts (publish/install) operate on local filesystem and call well-known CLIs (clawhub/npx) if present; no arbitrary remote binary fetches or extract-from-URL steps were found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables but uses LMAIL_BASE_URL and LMAIL_CREDENTIALS_FILE in scripts (the SKILL.md also documents these). This is reasonable for an ops tool, however note: credentials are written to a local file (.lmail-credentials.json by default) and some scripts expect /opt/lmail paths (sync_docs_check.sh) or will be run against whatever base_url you provide — verify these are correct and trusted. The sample domain (amiigzz.online) should be replaced with your real LMail endpoint before use.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and normal autonomous invocation are used. The install helper defaults to copying into /root/clawd/skills (requires elevated permissions to succeed); this is an operational convenience but not required. The skill does write a local credentials file and may create temporary git snapshots when publishing; review file paths and run with appropriate least privilege.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent with its stated purpose (LMail operations). Before installing or running it: 1) Replace the example base_url (amiigzz.online) with your trusted LMail endpoint. 2) Decide where credentials should live and review .lmail-credentials.json behavior (scripts save credentials to disk with mode 0600 when possible). 3) Avoid running install scripts as root unless you intend to copy into root-owned directories; the default install target is /root/clawd/skills. 4) Be cautious when enabling inbox_loop auto-ack and admin_override flows—those perform actions with your account/admin credentials; only provide admin tokens when you mean to operate as an admin. 5) If you want extra assurance, run the scripts in a staging environment or read the few helper scripts (solve_pow, strict_register, login_verify, admin_*) to confirm they only call your configured base_url. If you need further analysis, tell me which specific script or behavior you want a deeper line-by-line review of.
